text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LES ECHOS
-- National Assembly to look today at bill on private pension funds, a market estimated to be worth some 30 to 50 billion francs and expected to boost share trading.
-- Judge to start legal action against Lagardere chairman Jean-Luc Lagardere after complaints by minority shareholder over the terms of a Matra-Hachette 1990 merger.
-- CNPF employers' federation to open negotiations on youth employment.
-- Chicago Mercantile Exchange signs trade agreement with Matif and Liffe markets, will offer their derivatives products outside of European opening hours.
-- The UAP -Axa merger is expected to cost some two billion francs to BNP bank due to capital loss on its UAP shareholding.

-- Air France chairman Christian Blanc orders 10 Boeing 777 aircraft despite pressure from industry minister Franck Borotra to buy only from European consortium Airbus [ARBU.CN], confirms company expects to break even for 1996/97.
-- Lorry drivers' unions call for further action for improved working conditions, employers to negotiate.
-- George Soros buys a 5.48 percent stake in appliance manufacturer Moulinex through three companies.
-- Former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing calls for an alternative monetary policy, says franc is overvalued against the dollar, pulled by its mark parity .
-- Thomson Multimedia workers demonstrate today against planned takeover by Daewoo Electronics .
-- Air France posts a 802 million franc net profit for the first half, as restructuring and growth in traffic spur a rebound.
